chapters.through_line: A data structure is just a decision about how you lay things down. Every later cost follows from that one decision.

chapters.title: The Cost of Doing Things
chapters.through_line: Speed is not a feeling, it is a count. Learn to count steps and you can predict any system before you build it.

chapters.title: Arrays: The Row of Boxes
chapters.through_line: An array is fast because it is rigid. Every array problem is that rigidity showing its bill.

chapters.through_line: A linked list buys cheap insertion by giving up instant position. That single swap explains all of its behaviour.

chapters.through_line: Most systems are not about storing things, they are about deciding who gets served next. That rule is the structure.

chapters.through_line: Search is the price you pay for order you did not keep. Every search method is one trade: how much structure you maintain up front, against how fast you find later. Decide the structure first and the algorithm picks itself.

chapters.title: Sorting: Putting Things in Order
chapters.through_line: Sorting is never the goal. It is the investment you make so that every later question becomes cheap.

chapters.through_line: Hashing trades memory and order for the one thing nothing else gives you: an answer without a search.

chapters.through_line: A tree is what you get when one thing owns many things. Depth is the only number that decides its speed.

chapters.through_line: A binary search tree is binary search made permanent. It only keeps that promise while it stays balanced.
